english_retrieval.title: ‘Won’t back down’: Indian student protesters return after police crackdown - Al Jazeera
english_retrieval.snippet: *More than 100 students injured in police action against thousands of demonstrators during march on parliament. The heart of New Delhi – Parliament Street and Connaught Place, a colonial-era square – bears the imprint of Monday’s police crackdown on thousands of protesters, most of them students, who had shut down the capital, demanding that Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resign. After dark on Monday, Abhijeet Dipke – the leader of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a political pressure group that called the march – returned to a torn-down stage at the CJP’s main protest site near Jantar Mantar, an 18th-century observatory that is now an important location for protests. This is where more than 100 protesters from student unions have been sleeping for nearly a month to join Sonam Wangchuk, a prominent activist, on a hunger strike to seek the minister’s resignation.

english_retrieval.title: New Delhi Air Pollution Index Further Pushes for EV Adoption in India - CleanTechnica
english_retrieval.snippet: # New Delhi Air Pollution Index Further Pushes for EV Adoption in India. India’s latest push toward electric vehicles is being driven by more than industrial policy or climate commitments. It is also a response to one of the country’s most persistent public‑health crises: air pollution. The Delhi government has approved a sweeping new electric‑vehicle policy that offers owners of older vehicles more than US$1,000 to scrap their cars and replace them with battery‑electric models. Delhi’s struggle with air pollution is well‑documented by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), India’s official air‑quality regulator. Through the National Clean Air Programme’s PRANA portal, the CPCB tracks air‑quality trends and the implementation of clean‑air action plans across more than 130 non‑attainment cities—urban areas that consistently fail to meet national standards. On its official website, the government describes the EV Policy as one of the world’s most progressive because its central objective is to “drastically reduce vehicular air pollution” while positioning Delhi as a global leader in EV adoption.

english_retrieval.title: Big Relief For Private Schools! Delhi Govt Replaces Essentiality Certificate With Self-Certification System - ABP Live English
english_retrieval.snippet: Delhi Govt Replaces Essentiality Certificate With Self-Certification System. ## The Delhi government has replaced the Essentiality Certificate requirement with a self-certification system, simplifying the process for opening new private schools and reducing regulatory hurdles. Delhi replaces Essentiality Certificate with self-certification for schools. In a major policy reform, Delhi Education Minister Ashish Sood has approved the complete replacement of the "Essentiality Certificate" required to open private schools with a streamlined self-certification system, a press release stated. According to the press release from the office of Education Minister Ashish Sood, this reform follows the recommendations of the high-level Compliance Reduction and Deregulation Exercise, aimed at simplifying administrative procedures. Ashish Sood stated that this transition ensures Delhi's school recognition rules align strictly with the Central Government's Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009. In tandem with these procedural updates, the Delhi Government has also significantly relaxed the rigid minimum land area requirement previously mandated for the registration and setting up of private schools, the press release said.

english_retrieval.title: Delhi Government Replaces 'Essentiality Certificate' With Self-Certifications - NDTV
english_retrieval.snippet: # Delhi Government Replaces 'Essentiality Certificate' With Self-Certifications. ## New rules align Delhi's school recognition with RTE Act, focusing on infrastructure, teacher qualifications, and safety standards. Delhi introduces self-certification in place of Essentiality Certificate for private schools. * Delhi replaces Essentiality Certificate with self-certification for private schools. * New rules align with RTE Act focusing on infrastructure and teacher standards. The Delhi government has approved a major change in the process for opening private schools by replacing the long-standing 'Essentiality Certificate' requirement with a self-certification system. According to ANI, Delhi Education Minister Ashish Sood has approved the reform, under which the Directorate of Education will remove several outdated provisions under the Delhi School Education Act and Rules (DSER), 1973. Under the new system, private schools will no longer have to obtain an Essentiality Certificate, which earlier required government approval on whether a new school was needed in a particular area.
